articles.title: Scientists find nine new sponge species in glimpse of Alaska’s deep-sea diversity
articles.description: But their habitat is threatened by bottom trawling in the region and Trump’s plan to expand seafloor mining Scientists have discovered nine new deep-sea sponge species off Alaska, offering new insights into the region’s largely unexplored marine biodiversity. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) announced the discovery on Thursday, saying the species were found in the Gulf of Alaska and the Aleutian Islands. The findings bring the total number of known sponge species in Alaska to 232. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Immature playground boasting’: Mathematicians uneasy at OpenAI’s latest scalp
articles.description: As OpenAI model cracks Millennium Prize Problem that puzzled experts for decades, many feel shocked at pace of change It was a week that left mathematicians reeling. Hot on the heels of a flurry of cases of artificial intelligence furthering the field, OpenAI declared a major scalp: its latest AI model had cracked a Millennium Prize Problem, a puzzle with a $1m reward that had defied human brains for decades. The achievement bore little resemblance to how mathematical problems normally fall. A near-trillion dollar private company had unleashed 10,000 agents – AI systems that carry out tasks autonomously – on the problem. The bill was estimated at $15m. Continue reading...

articles.title: Starwatch: A Venus-spotting challenge with a beautiful reward
articles.description: The bright planet and the young crescent moon will make an attractive pairing on Monday evening This week’s Starwatch is a challenge but a beautiful reward awaits for anyone who succeeds. The question is: how early in the evening can we find Venus? On Monday, the bright planet has a close encounter with a young crescent moon. The moon will be just over three days old with about 14% of its visible surface illuminated. Unfortunately for UK observers, the two make their closest approach during daylight, passing within a moon’s width of one another around lunchtime. Continue reading...

articles.title: Fossilized 10,000-year-old mastodon tooth found by California scientist
articles.description: Molar from large mammal that once lived in North America is in ‘immaculate condition’ after discovery in Bay Area A 10,000 year-old tooth in remarkable condition from an ancient Pacific mastodon, a large mammal that once inhabited North America, was recently discovered by a California scientist. Brigid Lynch, a geomorphologist, was working at a preserve in San Mateo county, when she stumbled across a peculiar rock. Continue reading...

articles.title: Live episode: how AI is reshaping our minds – podcast

source.name: Presented by Ian Sample, with Madeleine Finlay and Michael Safi; produced by Madeleine Finlay; executive producer Ellie Bury

articles.description: In this episode of Science Weekly, recorded in front of an audience at the London podcast festival on 3 September, Ian Sample hears from Michael Safi, the host of the Guardian’s chart-topping podcast about artificial intelligence, Black Box. In series two, Black Box: the chatbots, Michael meets people who have become convinced they have made scientific breakthroughs, cured diseases or invented new technologies using AI chatbots. Ian, Michael and Science Weekly’s co-host Madeleine Finlay explore the phenomenon labelled ‘AI psychosis’ and ask what it reveals about a technology now used by more than a billion people Listen to Black Box: the chatbots Support the Guardian: theguardian.com/sciencepod Continue reading...

articles.title: Indonesian foragers may have sucked on mind-altering nuts 25,000 years ago, research finds
articles.description: Analysis of two skeletons reveals tooth wear and traces of psychoactive substance in what may be earliest known evidence for human drug taking What may be the earliest known evidence for human drug taking has been traced to ancient Indonesian foragers who sucked on mind-altering nuts as long as 25,000 years ago. Analysis of two exceptionally rare skeletons from the Indonesian island of Sulawesi revealed dramatic tooth wear and traces of a psychoactive substance in the individuals’ remaining teeth, suggesting they routinely sucked on hard, abrasive betel nuts. Continue reading...

articles.title: One giant step: first known adult T rex footprints found in North Dakota
articles.description: The 23ft-long trackway, consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right, date from 66.5m years ago The first known series of footprints from an adult Tyrannosaurus rex has been found in North Dakota by a team of scientists. The 23ft-long trackway – consisting of four three-toed footprints, two left and two right – was first identified in the south-west of the state, in the dinosaur fossil area known as Hell Creek Formation, last year by researchers from the Denver Museum of Nature and Science in Colorado and Liverpool John Moores University in the UK. Continue reading...

articles.title: Ebola outbreak in DRC has peaked, say authorities, as infection rates slow
articles.description: Almost 3,500 people have died in outbreak and experts say more must be done to ensure Bundibugyo is under control Authorities in the Democratic Republic of the Congo have announced that the Ebola outbreak ravaging parts of the country has reached its peak. For the first time since the epidemic was declared in May, the numbers of people becoming infected is slowing down, according to officials. Continue reading...

articles.title: Scientists find nine new sponge species in glimpse of Alaska’s deep-sea diversity
articles.description: But their habitat is threatened by bottom trawling in the region and Trump’s plan to expand seafloor mining Scientists have discovered nine new deep-sea sponge species off Alaska, offering new insights into the region’s largely unexplored marine biodiversity. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (Noaa) announced the discovery on Thursday, saying the species were found in the Gulf of Alaska and the Aleutian Islands. The findings bring the total number of known sponge species in Alaska to 232. Continue reading...

articles.title: ‘Immature playground boasting’: Mathematicians uneasy at OpenAI’s latest scalp
articles.description: As OpenAI model cracks Millennium Prize Problem that puzzled experts for decades, many feel shocked at pace of change It was a week that left mathematicians reeling. Hot on the heels of a flurry of cases of artificial intelligence furthering the field, OpenAI declared a major scalp: its latest AI model had cracked a Millennium Prize Problem, a puzzle with a $1m reward that had defied human brains for decades. The achievement bore little resemblance to how mathematical problems normally fall. A near-trillion dollar private company had unleashed 10,000 agents – AI systems that carry out tasks autonomously – on the problem. The bill was estimated at $15m. Continue reading...

articles.title: Why are there concerns AI could threaten humanity, and how real are they?
articles.description: Existential fears about AI have once again reared their head - here's what you need to know.

articles.title: Trump downplays warnings of AI risks, citing rivalry with China
articles.description: The US president said "negative forces" were airing concerns about "things that won't happen".

articles.title: Questions mount over what an AI 'slowdown' would look like
articles.description: While pacing AI development might sound like a quick fix, it is far from an easy solution.

articles.title: AI staff 'genuinely frightened' for humanity's future, ex-Anthropic researcher tells BBC
articles.description: It comes as the AI firm's boss has called for the technology's development to be slowed down, citing "serious" risks.

articles.title: Anthropic boss Dario Amodei calls for AI development to slow down
articles.description: The call comes amid growing concerns that AI models may become able to inflict serious damage worldwide.

articles.title: Pubs in England and Wales to allow digital ID apps to prove age
articles.description: New rules introduced on Tuesday mean establishments will be able to accept digital ID apps alongside physical documents.

articles.title: Valve's Steam Frame is excellent - but at over £1,000 is VR still too expensive?
articles.description: The BBC's Tom Gerken is hands-on with the latest virtual reality headset.
